The pictures are taken at the New York Presbyterian hospital downtown (Gold St as per the sign). The first is taken from a narrow angle to the left of the ambulance entrance. The second is taken from the side of the ambulance looking into the entrance to the hospital. There is a very small window of time (maybe 10 seconds) to get that second shot before the automatic doors close.

So here's what I noticed:

(1) The paramedics are attempting to resuscitate a corpse (supposedly). This is not possible. Once a good few minutes after death has passed the body stiffens quickly and it wouldn't be possible to inflate the lungs with a bag-and-mask (ambu-bag).

(2) If you were going to try to ventilate a dead/dying patient, you have to bring the lower jaw forward and keep it forward with two hands. Anaesthetists (anaesthesiologists) can do this with one hand because they have been doing it for years, but paramedics are not used to it. The picture shows the ambu-bag placed on the face with no effort to hold it in place. It would be useless on an unconscious person let alone a corpse. The amount of effort required to ventilate a corpse would be huge. For an unconscious patient receiving CPR it would be possible to ventilate them with this equipment but you would need two hands for the mask (as well as help from other people to do the chest compressions etc)

(3) The left arm of Epstein is outside the rail of the trolley and bent. These rails are elevated once the patient is on the trolley. If the person is dead or unconscious their arms flop out to the side. It is not possible for the arm to be bent unless the patient is conscious or it has been fixed to the rail.

(4) The only way this picture could happen with a dead person is if they handcuffed the arm to the rail (because of (3)). NO paramedic would do this if they were genuinely resuscitating a person. Not a chance. If you are really doing resuscitation it is all on to keep a heart beat going and to ventilate the patient. The last thing a paramedic would do is handcuff a hand to a bed rail. Apart from anything it would get in the way of a resuscitation and make it impossible to insert cannulas for drugs.

I know when the paramedics show up on the scene they do a quick evaluation to determine if the patient is dead and resuscitation would be futile. Is patient the breathing, have a pulse, cold to touch? If he is cold, he has been dead a while. If the body is still warm, you don't know how long the patient has been down so they would try to resuscitate. They would intubate, start chest compressions, place pads for cardiac monitor, get a IV, administer epinephrine. The paramedics are in constant contact with a doctor who is making decisions based on the details he is getting from the paramedics at the scene.
